title: $20 List Price?  Don't Make Me LOL.
text:
$20 List Price? Don't Make Me LOL.. That's not the selling price here, of course, but, to be honest, this timer isn't worth the selling price. It would be worth about half of that, maybe less. It works just fine, and it does have an easel and magnet on the back, but if you set it for an hour, you have to hear it beep 60 times as you click through the minutes.

The other thing I just really hate about it is that you have to push two buttons at once to clear the timer. I know, First World Problems, right? But it's too small & lightweight to press both buttons while it's propped up, and when you pick it up and hold it in your hand, and can't reset it with your thumb, so you suddenly need two hands to reset it to zero. We're not launching nuclear weapons here. I found it awkward and inconvenient in a busy kitchen.

When I browse through the kitchen timers on Amazon, it's easy to see that this one costs significantly more than most, and that's my main problem with this product. It works, but there is absolutely nothing about it that justifies the higher price. It's called Presto because you'll eventually want it to disappear.

product_metadata.title: Presto 04213 Electronic Digital Timer, White
features: This electronic digital timer counts down from any time up to 99 minutes and 59 seconds and has an alarm that signals when time is up
Timer also counts up for use as a handy stopwatch
Easy-to-read digital display shows minutes and seconds
Operates on one easy-to-find AAA battery; Battery included
Memory feature stores the last timer setting for quick repeat use; Convenient clip, easel stand, and magnet on back for versatile use
description: Some purist cooks claim to have an instinctive inner timer, but most people need a little help remembering when to take the roast out or punch down the bread dough for its second rise. This electronic timer fulfills that basic function. With an easy-to-read LCD display that shows minutes and seconds, the unit counts down from any time up to 99 minutes and 59 seconds. There's also a stopwatch function that's useful in many ways, and not necessarily only in the kitchen. An alarm signals when the time is up, and the memory function stores the last countdown time for reuse. The timer's versatile clip can also become an easel stand, and it has a magnet, too--it's good to go wherever it's needed. The handy gadget operates on one AAA battery, and it can be carefully wiped clean with a slightly damp rag as needed. The timer measures 2-1/2 by 2-1/4 by 1/2 inches.
